meaning: Number of descendants from Lod, Hadid and Ono upon returning from exile
description: The number 725 appears in Ezra 2:33, indicating the number of descendants from the cities of Lod, Hadid and Ono who returned from the Babylonian exile. These three cities were located in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin near the coastal plain, and their inhabitants' return testifies to the rebuilding of Jewish settlement after the exile. Beyond this specific occurrence, the number 725 does not have a well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition, nor is it highlighted with a specific numerological interpretation in gematria.

versions.meaning: The number 725 has no well-established or known symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 725 is not a number highlighted in the Bible or in traditional Jewish numerology (gematria) with a specific symbolic meaning. Historically, the year 725 BC is linked to the Assyrian siege of Samaria under Shalmaneser V, which is relevant to biblical history, but the number itself is not attributed any independent symbolic value. In gematria, individual letter combinations can sum to 725, but there is no widely recognized symbolic interpretation of this number.

footnotes.text: The year 725 BC is historically linked to the Assyrian siege of Samaria under Shalmaneser V (2 Kings 17:5), which led to the fall of the Northern Kingdom in 722 BC. Although the year is significant in biblical history, the number 725 itself is not attributed any independent symbolic value.

Lod (later Lydda) is known from both Old and New Testament times (Acts 9:32–35). Hadid and Ono are also mentioned in Nehemiah 7:37 and 11:35, and all three cities were strategically located in the Shephelah region.
